334808.title: Non-realizability conjecture for complete bipartite strong resolving graphs
334808.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $G_{SR}$ denote its strong resolving graph, whose vertices are the mutually maximally distant vertices of $G$, with adjacency between distinct mutually maximally distant vertices. For integers $r,s\ge 2$, consider the graph equation

$$
G_{SR}\cong K_{r,s}.
$$

**Complete bipartite strong resolving graph conjecture.** The graph equation $G_{SR}\cong K_{r,s}$ has no solution for any $r,s\ge 2$.

This conjecture extends the known non-realizability of the equations $G_{SR}\cong K_{1,r}$ and $G_{SR}\cong K_{2,r}$ for $r\ge 2$. It asks whether no complete bipartite graph with both parts of size at least two can occur as a strong resolving graph.
334808.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1612.02843v1 read: Sections 1.3 and 2 (MMD/boundary definitions, Remark 2, Lemmas 8-9, Theorem 10, Proposition 16, Conjecture 17). Prior art: arXiv:2008.04282 body read (Section on realization, p. with refs [5]); the cited note itself not fetched.
334808.disposition: Conjecture 17 (G_SR on the boundary is never K_{r,s}, r,s>=2) is TRUE and already settled: R. Lenin, "A short note on: There is no graph G with G_SR = K_{r,s}", Discrete Appl. Math. 265 (2019) 204-205, cited as the settlement in arXiv:2008.04282 ("Their conjecture was settled in [5]"). This lane independently found a one-paragraph proof (NOTES.md section 1): maximal geodesic extension of v1 v v2 gives an MMD pair x,y with v not MMD to either, contradicting complete bipartiteness unless every boundary vertex is simplicial, whence G_SR is complete (source Theorem 10). The proof uses only the source Lemma 8/9 idea plus a standard strengthening, so it would be zero credit even without the 2019 note.
334808.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Exact MMD/boundary computation (scripts/srg_lib.py, srg_search.py; self-test reproduces source Figure 5, C5, C6, trees, K33). Exhaustive over all connected graphs of orders 4-9 (6+21+112+853+11117+261080 graphs, McKay lists) and the first 3,000,000 of the 11,716,571 connected order-10 graphs (chunks 0-2,999,999 of graph10c.g6.gz): 0 realizations; search stopped after the prior-art finding. Logs logs/srg-*.
334808.prior_resolution: Lenin, DAM 265 (2019) 204-205, via arXiv:2008.04282 ref [5] (sources/prior-2008.04282.pdf sha256 470fe6cf...)

334872.title: RNC completeness conjecture for MDS extensions
334872.literal_statement: Let $q$ be a prime power and let $m$ be an integer for which the stated MDS codes are defined. An $[q+1,m]_q$ Reed–Solomon code corresponds to a normal rational curve (RNC) in $PG(m-1,q)$, and an MDS extension by one coordinate is an $[q+2,m]_q$ MDS code extending it. **RNC completeness conjecture.** There is no $[q+2,m]_q$ MDS code extending an $[q+1,m]_q$ Reed–Solomon code, except when $q$ is even and $m=3$ or $m=q-1$; equivalently, the RNC in $PG(m-1,q)$ is a complete arc except in those cases. The source notes that this conjecture is implied by the MDS conjecture and proves that the preceding MDS-extension conjecture implies it.
334872.review_depth: Abstract/current version (v1 only) read; MathDB literal statement.
334872.disposition: RNC completeness for MDS extensions of Reed-Solomon codes: implied by the MDS conjecture; Ball (q prime) and Ball-De Beule (k <= 2p-2) settle large families, but the general q = p^h case is open. No finite certificate can refute it (verified small-q classifications agree), and a proof is an MDS-conjecture-level problem.
334872.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: No computation (search space would be arc classification in PG(m-1,q); known tables already consistent).
334872.precise_remaining_gap: Full MDS-type extension classification for non-prime q and large m.

334925.title: Almost fair representation conjecture for dimatroids
334925.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ and $\mathcal Q$ be matroids on the same ground set $V$, let $\mathcal D=\mathcal P\cap\mathcal Q$, and set

$$
\zeta=\max\bigl(\zeta(\mathcal P),\zeta(\mathcal Q)\bigr).
$$

A set $S$ represents a part $A$ almost $\alpha$-fairly when $|S\cap A|\ge \lfloor\alpha|A|\rfloor-1$. **Almost fair representation conjecture.** Every partition of $V$ has an almost $1/\zeta$-fair representation by a set in $\mathcal D$. The conjecture extends the corresponding matroid representation theorem to dimatroids. The paper notes that the exact $1/\zeta$ bound is impossible for the matching complex of $C_4$, and records partial results for intersections of two partition matroids with parts of size $2$; the general claim remains open in the supplied text.
334925.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1612.07652v3 Sections 1-2 read (Conjecture 2.2, Theorems 1.6, 2.1, 2.3, 2.7, Example 2.6); v1 also fetched.
334925.disposition: Almost 1/zeta-fair representation in dimatroids. Source proves partitions into two sets (Theorem 2.7, slightly weaker) and the two-partition-matroids-with-parts-of-size-2 case. For bipartite matching complexes (zeta = max degree Delta) a counterexample needs at least two parts of size >= 2 Delta with requirement >= 1; for two parts an edge meets at most 2 Delta - 1 edges, so two-part violations are impossible; total requirement sum |A_i|/Delta - m is below nu >= |E|/Delta by m, so small counterexamples are implausible. Not settled.
334925.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Analytic slack argument only; no exhaustive matroid enumeration (no matroid database in lane; pure-python enumeration of matroid pairs beyond 7 elements infeasible under caps).
334925.precise_remaining_gap: General dimatroid exchange lemma (source Conjecture 4.2) or an explicit multi-part obstruction.

339813.title: Kotěšovec's Fibonacci-period conjecture for queens
339813.literal_statement:
Let $F_q$ be the $q$th Fibonacci number, let $[F_q]=\{1,2,\ldots,F_q\}$, and let $u_{\mathbb Q}(q;n)$ be the counting quasipolynomial for $q$ queens. **Kotěšovec's conjecture.** The period of $u_{\mathbb Q}(q;n)$ is

$$
\operatorname{lcm}[F_q],
$$

the least common multiple of all positive integers up through $F_q$. Kotěšovec's conjectured periods through $q=7$ agree with this formula, but the general assertion is not proved in the supplied text.
339813.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1807.04741v1 Sections 2 and 6 read (Conjectures 2.4, 6.4, 6.5); sibling records 339810/339812 parked by fresh-corpus-r20.
339813.disposition: Kotesovec period lcm[F_q] (F_0=F_1=1). Periods themselves are known only empirically (Kotesovec data through q=7 agrees). A refutation needs the exact period of the q=8 queens quasipolynomial; a proof needs the denominator conjecture 6.5 plus period = denominator (Conjecture 2.4). No finite certificate within reach; Lean formalization of inside-out Ehrhart quasipolynomial periods is far beyond campaign cost.
339813.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: None beyond source reading (r20 already tried exact vertex systems for the sibling denominator conjecture).
339813.precise_remaining_gap: Exact period computation for q=8 or a structural Fibonacci-denominator theorem.

329577.title: Divisibility conjecture for shifted sums involving $R_{k,r}$
329577.literal_statement:
For positive integers $n$ and $r$, define

$$
R_{n,r}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}{n+k\choose 2k}{2k\choose k}\frac{1}{2k-2r-1}.
$$

**Divisibility conjecture for shifted sums.** There exists an integer $a_r$, independent of $n$, such that

$$
a_r\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(2k+1)R_{k,r}^2\equiv 0\pmod n.
$$

This is motivated by numerical calculation and asserts uniform divisibility after multiplication by a constant depending only on $r$. The source gives no proof or resolution.
329577.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1501.00573v1 read (Conjecture 5.3 and the remark a_r=(2r+1)!!^2; Sections 1-2 method). Web search found no later proof (Mao arXiv:1511.06221 settles Conjecture 5.2, not 5.3).
329577.disposition: Guo-Liu Conjecture 5.3. Exact rational computation (scripts/r329577.py) of the least a_r(N) = lcm_{n<=N} denominator(S_n/n) for r=0..7, N=120: a_r stabilises at 1, 9, 225, 3675, 99225, 2401245, 135270135, 289864575 from n<=10 onward, each dividing (2r+1)!!^2. Conjecture strongly supported. Christoffel-Darboux for shifted Legendre polynomials gives S_n = n (L_r x L_r)(Q_n)/2 with Q_n integral (NOTES.md section 4), which explains the factor n but not the bounded denominator. A uniform proof would most likely follow the source multivariable-Zeilberger plus binomial-divisibility route: high risk of the same routine-source-adaptation exclusion as the root Guo divisibility ruling (lanes/root-guo-divisibility-review-adoption-r1/DECISION.md), and Lean-heavy.
329577.precise_remaining_gap: A uniform-in-r denominator bound for (L_r x L_r)(Q_n)/2, i.e. (2r+1)!!^2-integrality for all n.

329610.title: Existence of an extremizer for the proposed Mahler-volume lower bound
329610.literal_statement:
Let $n\geq 4$, let $K$ be a symmetric convex set in $\mathbb{R}^n$, let $K^{\circ}$ denote its polar body, and let $\alpha(n)$ be the constant defined earlier in the source. The $n$-dimensional volume is denoted by $\operatorname{vol}_n$, and $\Gamma$ is the Gamma function.

**Existence conjecture.** There is a symmetric convex set $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ such that

$$
\operatorname{vol}_n(K)\operatorname{vol}_n(K^{\circ})=\frac{4\alpha(n-1)\pi^n}{\Gamma\left(\frac{n}{2}\right)^2}.
$$

This conjecture asks whether the lower bound supplied by the paper's theorem is attained in every dimension $n\geq 4$. The source does not provide a resolution, and the notation $\alpha(n)$ is defined elsewhere in the paper.
329610.review_depth: Abstract and current version (v2, 2018) read; body not read.
329610.disposition: Attainment of a Mahler-volume lower bound defined through a source-specific variational constant alpha(n); analytic convex geometry, outside the finite-certificate scope; the literal statement depends on the unrecovered definition of alpha(n).
329610.precise_remaining_gap: Recover alpha(n) and decide whether the localisation bound is sharp.

329760.title: The partial-sum sequencing conjecture for subsets of cyclic groups
329760.literal_statement:
Let $A=a_1,ots,a_k$ be a subset of the nonzero elements of ${\mathbb Z}_n$. For an ordering $(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ of $A$, define the partial sums by

$$
s_j=\sum_{i=1}^j a_i\qquad (1\leq j\leq k),
$$

with arithmetic in ${\mathbb Z}_n$. **Partial-sum sequencing conjecture.** There exists an ordering of the elements of $A$ such that the partial sums are all distinct; equivalently, $s_i\ne s_j$ whenever $1\leq i<j\leq k$. This conjecture generalizes sequencing questions for cyclic groups and is motivated by cyclic cycle systems and embeddings of complete graphs on surfaces. The source reports partial results: the claim is known for $k\leq5$, for $n\leq16$, and for $k=n-1$ or $k=n-2$ via the related Alspach conjecture. The general case remains open.
329760.review_depth: Abstract read; MathDB statement; literature status via web search (source verified n<=25 by randomised guess-and-check and k<=6 by proof; Hicks-Ollis-Schmitt arXiv:1809.02684 polynomial method). Sibling 329765/329766 parked by fresh-corpus-r9.
329760.disposition: Archdeacon-Dinitz-Mattern-Stinson partial-sum sequencing (contains Alspach-type sequencing). Large partial-resolution literature (family warning); counterexample search beyond n=25 needs all subsets of Z_n with an ordering search per subset (2^25 subsets), infeasible under lane caps; no exact mechanism for a full proof.
329760.precise_remaining_gap: Uniform proof for all k in all cyclic groups.

330216.title: The bipartite Kneser graph Hamiltonicity conjecture
330216.literal_statement: For integers $n$ and $k$ with $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq 2k+1$, let the **bipartite Kneser graph** $H(n,k)$ have as vertices all $k$-element and all $(n-k)$-element subsets of $[n]:=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$, with an edge between two vertices exactly when one corresponding set is a subset of the other. **Bipartite Kneser graph Hamiltonicity conjecture.** For any $k\geq 1$ and $n\geq 2k+1$, the bipartite Kneser graph $H(n,k)$ has a Hamilton cycle. The conjecture is presented as a longstanding Hamiltonicity problem; no resolution is supplied in the source.
330216.review_depth: Abstract of the source itself read (v3, Combinatorica 37(6) 2017).
330216.disposition: The MathDB record says the source supplies no resolution, but the source IS the resolution: Muetze and Su, "Bipartite Kneser graphs are Hamiltonian", Combinatorica 37 (2017) 1207-1219, prove H(n,k) Hamiltonian for all k>=1, n>=2k+1. MathDB paraphrase defect; zero credit.

330252.title: The feedback vertex set bound for planar graphs of prescribed girth
330252.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple planar graph of size $m$ and **girth** $g$, where the girth is the length of a shortest cycle. A **feedback vertex set** is a set of vertices whose removal leaves an acyclic graph.

**Feedback vertex set conjecture for prescribed girth.** There exists a feedback vertex set $S$ of $G$ satisfying

$$
|S| \le \frac{m}{g}.
$$

Equivalently, $G$ has an induced forest with at least $|V(G)|-\frac{m}{g}$ vertices. The source presents this as a conjecture for planar graphs with given girth and provides no evidence of resolution.
330252.review_depth: Source abstract (v1) read; prior resolution body read by expanded-corpus-r71 (record 376135: arXiv:2607.17983 Theorem 1.6 and its proof via Theorems 1.4/1.5).
330252.disposition: fvs(G) <= m/g for planar graphs of girth g is the Dross-Montassier-Pinlou conjecture, confirmed in arXiv:2607.17983 (2026) via a planar signed-graph frustration bound; see expanded-corpus-r71/results.json 376135. Zero credit.

330285.title: Isomorphic-vertex conjecture for critical banned graphs
330285.literal_statement: Let a graph be **critical banned in dimension** $d$ when it is banned in dimension $d$ but deleting any vertex lowers the required dimension. Two vertices are isomorphic when deleting either one produces a graph of smaller dimension and the two resulting graphs are isomorphic. **The isomorphic-vertex conjecture.** Every graph critical banned in dimension $d$ has at least two isomorphic vertices. The source gives no proof or resolution.
330285.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1504.03662v2 Sections 1 and 3 read (Definitions 1.1-1.4, 3.1-3.2, Conjectures 3.1-3.3).
330285.disposition: The source defines "critical for dimension d" by EDGE removal (Definition 3.1) while Conjecture 3.2 and MathDB speak of vertex deletion; the faithful orthogonal rank rho_perp (real-algebraic) has no exact computable characterisation in the source, and its sample values (e.g. "Petersen banned to dim 2, rho_perp(P)=3") are unsupported. No well-posed finite target; note that any graph with a nontrivial automorphism trivially has two isomorphic vertices, so a counterexample must be vertex-deck-distinct and critical, which cannot be certified without an exact rho_perp oracle.
330285.precise_remaining_gap: A precise definition and an exact algorithm for rho_perp.

330593.title: Refined Kikuta–Ruckle conjecture
330593.literal_statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and $d\in(0,1)$. In the KR-Problem, an optimal solution has equal nonzero coordinates as in the Kikuta–Ruckle conjecture. Define $\lfloor x\rfloor$ and the parity-restricted floor functions exactly as in the source. **Refined Kikuta–Ruckle conjecture.** There is an optimal solution with

$$
a_1=\cdots=a_s=\frac1s,\qquad a_{s+1}=\cdots=a_n=0,
$$

where $s$ belongs to the displayed finite set in the source statement. This is presented as a stronger version of the Kikuta–Ruckle conjecture; its full characterization is not proved.
330593.review_depth: Abstract (v3) read; siblings 330598 (expanded-corpus-r80) and Ruckle items (expanded-corpus-r142) already parked.
330593.disposition: Refined Kikuta-Ruckle conjecture: continuous optimisation over probability vectors with source-displayed finite set for s; the literal record omits the set ("exactly as in the source"); the known Kikuta-Ruckle cases do not cover it. No finite certificate.
330593.precise_remaining_gap: Optimality of equal-weight solutions for all (n,k,d).

330655.title: Exoo's conjecture on the chromatic number of epsilon-unit distance graphs
330655.literal_statement:
Let $G_\varepsilon$ be the graph with vertex set $\mathbb{R}^2$ in which two points are adjacent when their distance $d$ satisfies $1-\varepsilon\leq d\leq 1+\varepsilon$, and let $\chi(G_\varepsilon)$ denote its chromatic number. **Exoo's conjecture.** For any $\varepsilon>0$,

$$
\chi(G_\varepsilon)=7.
$$

Exoo's computational work suggested that the exact chromatic number is $7$ for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$; the stated universal claim is presented as a conjectural extension of the known results, which establish exact values for some ranges and lower bounds for others.
330655.disposition: Exoo conjectured chi(G_[a,b])=7 only for SUFFICIENTLY SMALL positive b-a. The MathDB "for any epsilon>0" is trivially false: for epsilon>=1 every two points at distance <=2 are adjacent, so a unit disc is an uncountable clique and chi is infinite. That literal refutation is a zero-credit wording correction; the intended small-epsilon conjecture is open (source proves chi>=5).
330655.precise_remaining_gap: Intended statement: chi(G_eps)=7 for all small eps (needs >=7 lower bound; open).

330666.title: Conjecture on linear perfect codes in the $l_2$ metric
330666.literal_statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $r>0$, and let $\Lambda$ be an additive subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}^n$. A **linear perfect code** in the $\ell_p$ metric is such a subgroup whose translates tile $\mathbb{Z}^n$ by the balls

$$
B_p^n(r)=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^n:|x_1|^p+\cdots+|x_n|^p\leq r^p\right\}.
$$

**Conjecture.** There are no linear perfect codes with parameters $(n,r,2)$ except when $r=1$ or

$$
(n,r)\in\left\{(2,\sqrt{2}),(2,2),(2,2\sqrt{2}),(3,\sqrt{3})\right\}.
$$

In particular, there are no linear perfect codes in the $\ell_2$ metric if $n>3$ and $r>1$. The claim is motivated by computational evidence and by the absence of cubic polyominoes in the relevant higher-dimensional cases; it remains open in the source.
330666.disposition: Nonexistence of linear perfect l2 codes for n>3, r>1: infinite family in dimension and radius; source settles n=2,3 and gives packing bounds. No finite counterexample mechanism (existence would need a lattice tiling by a discrete l2 ball in dimension >=4, contradicting known polyomino-tiling evidence); proof needs new geometry.

330713.title: Lee–Zhang conjecture on length-spectrum domination by Fuchsian representations
330713.literal_statement:
Let $S$ be a connected closed oriented surface with fundamental group $amma$, and let $L_\rho$ denote the length spectrum of a representation with respect to the specified invariant Finsler metric on the symmetric space $\operatorname{PSL}(n,\mathbb{R})/\operatorname{PSO}(n)$. A representation $\rho:\Gamma\to\operatorname{PSL}(n,\mathbb{R})$ is **Hitchin**, and $j$ is **Fuchsian**, as in the source.

**Lee–Zhang conjecture.** For any Hitchin representation $\rho:\Gamma\to\operatorname{PSL}(n,\mathbb{R})$, there is a Fuchsian representation $j$ such that

$$
L_j\leq L_\rho.
$$

The conjecture would imply a sharper collar lemma for Hitchin representations. It is proved in the source when $n=3$, but Labourie explained that it cannot hold for $n\geq4$, so the conjecture is refuted in general.
330713.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1506.04640v2 introduction read (Theorem 3, Conjecture (Lee-Zhang), Labourie remark).
330713.disposition: Source proves the n=3 case (Theorem 3) and records Labourie's explanation that the Lee-Zhang conjecture fails for n>=4 (Hitchin representations into PSp(2k,R), PSO(k,k+1)); the general statement is thus already refuted in the source and a modified conjecture is proposed. Zero credit.

331313.title: Conjecture on partitioning a dense graph into two dense spanning subgraphs
331313.literal_statement:
Let $s,t\geq 0$ be real numbers, and let $G$ be a non-null graph. A subgraph is $s$-dense if it has at least $s$ edges per vertex.

**Partition conjecture.** If

$$
e(G)\geq (s+t+1)v(G),
$$

then there exist vertex-disjoint non-null subgraphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that

$$
e(G_1)\geq sv(G_1),\qquad e(G_2)\geq tv(G_2),
$$

and

$$
V(G_1)\cup V(G_2)=V(G).
$$

The conjecture would strengthen several aspects of the paper's main theorem and implies another conjecture in the paper. The supplied text records partial results when $s=t$ or when $e(G)\geq(s+t+\frac32)v(G)$, but does not state a complete resolution.
331313.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1509.01185v1 Section 4 read (Conjecture 12, Theorem 13 Wu). Prior resolution: arXiv:2202.08123 abstract read (Wang and Wu, JCTB 2024 per web search).
331313.disposition: Conjecture 12 is proved in full by Yan Wang and Hehui Wu, "Graph partitions under average degree constraint" (arXiv:2202.08123): every graph of average degree >= s+t+2 has a vertex bipartition with parts of average degree >= s and >= t, i.e. exactly e(G)>=(s+t+1)v(G) => e(G[A])>=s|A|, e(G[B])>=t|B| after halving s,t. Zero credit.
331313.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Exact staircase checker (scripts/dense_part.py, exact rationals, all 2^n-2 bipartitions; worst (s,t) at Pareto corners) on all connected graphs of orders 4-9 (273,189 graphs): 0 violations; minimum slack 0 attained only by K_n (corner-tight), next 1/n by K_n minus an edge. Logs logs/dense-*.

331481.title: Dimension-free stability conjecture for the uniform cover inequality
331481.literal_statement:
Let $d\in\mathbb{N}$ with $d\geq 2$, let $S\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$ be finite, and let ${\cal G}$ be the uniform cover family with projection maps $\pi_g$, covering multiplicity $m({\cal G})$, and stability parameter $\rho({\cal G})$. If

$$
|S|\geq (1-\epsilon)\left(\prod_{g\in{\cal G}}|\pi_g S|\right)^{1/m({\cal G})},
$$

then **the dimension-free uniform cover stability conjecture.** There exists a box $B\subset\mathbb{Z}^d$ such that

$$
|S\mathbin{\Delta}B|\leq c\,\rho({\cal G})\epsilon\,|S|,
$$

where $c$ is an absolute constant. This conjecture proposes removing the dependence on $d$ from the paper's uniform cover stability theorem, strengthening quantitative control of near-extremal sets.
331481.disposition: Dimension-free constant in uniform-cover stability: analytic/information-theoretic, asymptotic in d; outside finite-certificate scope.

331535.title: The regular edge-connected cycle cover conjecture
331535.literal_statement:
Let $k$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a $k$-regular, $(k-1)$-edge-connected graph. A **cycle $(k-1)$-cover** is a list of cycles in $G$ in which every edge appears exactly $k-1$ times.

**Regular edge-connected cycle cover conjecture.** There exists a cycle $(k-1)$-cover of $G$.

The paper presents this as a suspected extension of its technique to cycle $k$-covers. No resolution is given, so the statement remains open.
331535.review_depth: Source abstract and author error note (v2) read; sibling 331534 parked by expanded-corpus-r138. Public prior: openai/cdc-lean README and Main.lean endpoint read (not rebuilt).
331535.disposition: For k=3 the statement is the cycle double cover conjecture for cubic bridgeless graphs. The CDC theorem is now public with a kernel-checked Lean endpoint: openai/cdc-lean (created 2026-06-24, last push 2026-07-09), theorem CDCLean.cycleDoubleCover_of_bridgeless : Nonempty G.CycleDoubleCover for every finite loopless bridgeless multigraph (via Jaeger-Kilpatrick eight-flow and cubic expansion); also indexed in Lean Pool candidates (jarfo/cdc-statements etc.). The full regular statement then follows routinely (NOTES.md section 3): k odd: (k-1)/2 copies of a CDC; k even: the k-regular graph is Eulerian, so a circuit decomposition plus (k-2)/2 copies of a CDC (k-1>=1 gives bridgeless for k>=2; k<=2 trivial). Zero credit.
331535.precise_remaining_gap: None (subject to the public CDC proof; its body was not audited here).

331543.title: The chromatic-number bound for Latin square graphs
331543.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbf L$ be a Latin square of order $n$, and let $\chi(\mathbf L)$ denote the chromatic number of its Latin square graph. Then

**The chromatic-number conjecture.** Every Latin square $\mathbf L$ satisfies

$$
\chi(\mathbf L) \le \begin{cases} n+1 & \text{if $n$ is odd},\\ n+2 & \text{if $n$ is even.}\end{cases}
$$

For $n\le 8$ this bound is established in the paper; the conjecture is presented as challenging even for Cayley tables of groups. It would imply the Brualdi–Stein and Ryser conjectures on long transversals.
331543.review_depth: Abstract (v2) read; status via web search (Goddyn-Halasz: abelian Cayley tables have chi = n or n+2, and chi(L) = n + o(n); cyclic case simplified arXiv:2109.01194).
331543.disposition: Latin-square chromatic bound implies Brualdi-Stein and Ryser-type transversal conjectures; source verified n<=8 for all main classes. Exhaustive extension to n=9 (about 1.93e10 main classes) with exact chromatic number is far beyond Python caps; Latin squares are an already-credited family (381433, 347712). Park.

331819.title: Hamilton path conjecture for connected graphs with exactly two spanning paths after vertex deletion
331819.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n\geq 2$ vertices. Here, $\psi_k(G)$ denotes the number of paths in $G$ with $k$ vertices.

**Hamilton path conjecture.** The following implication holds

$$
\psi_{n-1}(G)=2 \Rightarrow \psi_n(G)=1.
$$

The conjecture asserts that a connected graph with exactly two paths on $n-1$ vertices must contain a Hamilton path. It was proposed from computational data for graphs with up to nine vertices, and the source states that, to the authors' knowledge, it had not previously been studied.
331819.review_depth: Primary source arXiv:1511.05384v1 read (abstract definitions; Section 4 Conjecture 4.4, Remark 4.5, Theorem 4.6).
331819.disposition: MathDB paraphrase defect: psi_k is the minimum k-path vertex cover number, not a path count (under the paraphrase a 5-vertex spider with legs 1,1,2 already refutes it, also zero credit). With the source definition, for n>=3: psi_{n-1}(G)=2 iff every vertex-deleted subgraph G-v is traceable (no single vertex meets all (n-1)-paths iff each G-v has a Hamilton path, and any two vertices always meet every (n-1)-path), and psi_n(G)=1 iff G is traceable. So Conjecture 4.4 is equivalent to the nonexistence of hypotraceable graphs, which exist classically (Horton 40-vertex example reported by Gruenbaum 1974; Thomassen, Discrete Math. 9 (1974) 91-96, 34 vertices). Refuted by a classical construction: zero credit (372630 precedent); also a 34+-vertex non-traceability certificate is Lean-expensive.
331819.mathematical_attempts_and_coverage: Equivalence proof (NOTES.md section 2); no computation needed.

331893.title: Warmth-index conjecture for graph homomorphism complexes
331893.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite graph. Write $\text{Hom}(K_2,G)$ for the homomorphism complex from the edge $K_2$ to $G$, and let $\operatorname{ind}(X)$ denote the least integer $m$ for which there exists a ${\mathbb Z}_2$-equivariant map from the ${\mathbb Z}_2$-space $X$ to the antipodal sphere ${\mathbb S}^m$. Let $\zeta(G)$ be the warmth of $G$. **Warmth-index conjecture.** One has

$$
\zeta(G)\leq \operatorname{ind}(\text{Hom}(K_2,G))+2.
$$
This is presented as a weaker version of the warmth-connectivity conjecture, since $\operatorname{conn}(X)+1\leq \operatorname{ind}(X)$. It would still imply the desired connection between warmth and a topological lower bound for the chromatic number; the paper leaves it open.
331893.disposition: Warmth <= ind(Hom(K2,G))+2: warmth is defined by asymptotics of d-branching walks and the Z2-index is topological; neither is finitely computable in general, so no finite certificate is available. Park.
331893.precise_remaining_gap: Topological lower bound linking warmth to Z2-index.
